subject: BlueWave - AWS private offer options & buyer approval lanes
messages:
From: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@bluewave.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ken Wu <ken.wu@bluewave.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BlueWave - AWS private offer options & buyer approval lanes

Hi Vanessa / Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week — BlueWave is excited about embedding Redwood for inference across our pipelines. Procurement asked for a clear set of options for an AWS Marketplace private offer so they can circulate internally. Two quick asks: 

1) Pricing & term options you can support (12 / 24 / 36 months) and whether we can do annual billing vs upfront?
2) Any special buyer-approval lanes or docs we should prepare (e.g., for deals > $250k their legal/security teams need to see SOC2 evidence and AWS buyer approvals sometimes add steps).

Attached: BlueWave_SOW_draft.pdf and our procurement policy (BlueWave_Procurement_Policy.pdf) — that should show routing and approval thresholds.

Can you let me know a recommended path so I can get internal buy-in? Prefer to keep this simple for our procurement team.

Best,
Sophie Tran
Head of Platform Partnerships
BlueWave Analytics
Attachments: BlueWave_SOW_draft.pdf (pdf), BlueWave_Procurement_Policy.pdf (pdf)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@bluewave.ai>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueWave - AWS private offer options & buyer approval lanes

Hi Sophie — great to connect. Short answer up front: we can support 12/24/36 month private offers, and we typically recommend 24 months for stability + negotiated discounts. Annual billing is possible with a 24- or 36-month term, but invoice cadence affects AWS billing and marketplace reconciliation (we'll coordinate with finance).

Quick notes for procurement routing:
- Deals under ~$50k: standard marketplace flow, usually no additional AWS approval.
- $50k–$250k: buyer org may request finance review; private offer still straightforward.
- > $250k: expect procurement + security signoffs; sometimes the buyer must request AWS to approve the private offer depending on their org settings.

What we recommend for BlueWave:
- Option A: 24-month term, annual invoicing, 15% commit discount (example).
- Option B: 12-month term, annual invoicing, 8% discount.
- Option C: 36-month term, annual or upfront, 20% discount with elevated commit and co-sell priority.

I'll loop Marcus (legal) and Laura (finance) to call out contract nuances and billing flow. Also attaching our internal playbook with runbook for building the AWS private offer: Redwood_PO_Playbook.pdf.

Next step: can you confirm desired term and total contract value range so we can draft the private offer and a mutual action plan?

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_PO_Playbook.pdf (pdf)

From: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@bluewave.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Ken Wu <ken.wu@bluewave.ai>, procurement@bluewave.ai
Date: 2027-05-04T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueWave - AWS private offer options & buyer approval lanes

Thanks Vanessa — that framework is exactly what procurement needs. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Likely target: Option A (24 months) with annual billing. We expect first-year annual spend ~ $320k; second-year similar.
- Procurement note: any PO over $300k triggers VP procurement + legal review and they will want SOC2 evidence and standard liability caps spelled out.
- Security: CISO team will require a short security questionnaire and the SOC2 report; can you share a recent SOC2 link or the security pack?

Can you also start a draft private offer so procurement can see the AWS SKU/offer metadata and routing? If you can include an estimate of when the buyer will see the offer in their AWS console, that will help our timeline.

Attaching our procurement policy for routing again.

Appreciate it — Sophie
Attachments: BlueWave_Procurement_Policy.pdf (pdf)

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-05T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueWave - AWS private offer options & buyer approval lanes

Summary of legal points after quick review:
- Term length: 24 months is fine. Recommend automatic renewal language with a 60-day opt-out notice rather than auto-renew to avoid procurement pushback.
- Billing cadence: annual invoicing is acceptable, but account for AWS Marketplace's settlement timing — finance will need to map invoice timing vs AWS payout.
- Liability & termination: ask to limit termination for convenience to 90 days with pro-rata refund for unused prepaid amounts if we accept upfront; otherwise standard 30-day termination for convenience on annual billing.
- Security: we can provide SOC2 Type II report and a short security addendum. Share the redlined PO template: Redwood_PO_Template_redlines.docx.

Action items I recommend now:
1) Draft the private offer in the AWS Marketplace console with the three term/price options. Include metadata that flags this as "Redwood co-sell eligible" so we can engage AWS sales if needed.
2) Prepare a concise security pack (SOC2 link + one-page answers) for BlueWave's CISO.
3) Laura to confirm invoice template and whether we can accept PO + Net30 for first-year invoicing.

I'll prepare the redlines for signature once we confirm the chosen option.

—Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_PO_Template_redlines.docx (docx)

From: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

- Marcus: finalize contract redlines (auto-renew opt-out window, termination language, security addendum).
- Laura: confirm we can invoice annually and accept PO + Net30; prepare the invoice template tied to the private offer ID.
- Evelyn (me): coordinate co-sell flagging with AWS if BlueWave wants prioritized buyer approval lane.

Sophie — can we lock a 30-minute call Thursday 5/13 at 11am PT to review the offer and walk procurement through the console preview? If that works I'll send a calendar invite.

Evelyn Hart
